subject: nutrition-food-science
title: Protein Denaturation: Egg White Sets
objectives: Describe protein denaturation in order: folded chains, unfolding, bonding into a network, set white
Explain why the set white still holds its water, trapped inside the protein network
Explain why gentle heat, not strong heat or drying, is what unfolds the chains in this change

definitions.meaning: The change in which heat unfolds folded protein chains so they bond into a network and the food sets, as when egg white turns opaque and firm.
The clear, runny part of the egg around the yolk; it is mostly water with protein chains folded inside it.
A long chain molecule in the egg white that starts folded into a tight coil and unfolds when heated.
A protein chain in raw white: coiled up tightly, so the white stays clear and runny (s1).
A protein chain after gentle heat has opened its coil out into a long loose chain, ready to bond (s2).
The net built when unfolded chains bond to each other; it gives the set white its firm structure (s3).
The water of the white held in the pockets of the protein network after setting - it never leaves the white.
The steady warmth from the pan that gives the folded chains the energy to unfold without scorching the white.
The finished white after s4: opaque, firm, holding its shape, with its water still trapped inside the network.

mechanismSteps: Raw, folded chains: raw egg white is clear and runny, and each protein chain inside it is folded into a tight coil (s1).
Unfolding, gentle heat: the pan warms gently and the heat gives the folded chains energy to open out into long loose chains (s2).
Bonding, network forms: the unfolded chains link to each other with new bonds, building a network that traps the water in its pockets as the white turns opaque (s3).
Set, water trapped: the white is fully set - opaque, firm and holding its shape - with the water still trapped inside its network (s4).
workedExample: Work one white stage by stage. Step 1 (s1): the raw white is clear and runny with its chains folded into tight coils. Step 2 (s2): gentle heat from the pan unfolds each coil into a long loose chain. Step 3 (s3): the unfolded chains bond to each other and form a network that traps the water inside it. Step 4 (s4): the white turns opaque and sets firm, holding its shape with its water still held in the network.

trap.misconception: The white sets because the heat dries the water out of it.
trap.explanation: The slip: The white does turn from clear and runny to opaque and firm as it cooks, so it is easy to assume the change must be water leaving - drying out feels like the obvious way for something runny to become solid. The fix: The water stays trapped in the protein network - heat unfolds the chains and they bond and set. Gentle heat unfolds the folded protein chains in the egg white, the unfolded chains bond to each other and form a network that traps the water inside it, and the white turns opaque and sets firm with its water still held in the network. In class, replay scene 3: freeze on the chains bonding into a network and ask where the water is in the picture - it is sitting in the pockets of the network, which is why the set white is moist and firm rather than dry.
